summary: Walther Michaelis was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber circa 1894–1898. He later served as Director at the Francke Foundations from 1931 to 1935.

Walther Prellwitz was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Adalbert Bezzenberger and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Königsberg (~1881–1885). He served there as Privatdozent in 1901 and ao. Professor of Comparative Linguistics in 1924.

Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied under Ernst Leumann at Strasbourg (Ph.D. ~1901–1904) and habilitated at Humboldt University of Berlin. He worked at the Royal Library of Berlin and held the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg (1920–1951).

Walther Wüst was an Indology and linguistics scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Munich (1920–1923), later serving there as Privatdozent and dean. He also held posts at the Ahnenerbe, Bavarian Academy of Sciences, and Deutsche Akademie.

Wanda Dynowska worked in religious studies, Indology, and Tibetology, having studied at the University of Lausanne. She served as general secretary of the Polish Theosophical Society in 1921 and founded the Indo-Polish Library in 1944.
Wang Pachow worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology. He studied under Tan Yun-shan and served on the teaching and research staff at Visva-Bharati University.

Wannaporn Rienjang is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Cambridge. Her posts include lecturer at Thammasat University (2019) and project assistant at the University of Oxford (attested 2019–2022).

Warren Crawford Cowgill was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his B.A. at Stanford under Hermann Fränkel and his Ph.D. at Yale under Paul Tedesco and Paul Thieme, later serving as an assistant professor at Yale from 1956 to 1972.
Warren Lee Todd is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned his PhD at Lancaster University under the doctoral supervision of Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad.

Warrin Ratanamalai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2007) under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni.

Waso Harada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Ryukoku University and Koyasan University. His academic posts include lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1999–2006) and visiting researcher at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2002–2007).

Watari Yanai was a scholar of sinology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1900 to 1903 and held a post there from circa 1908 to 1926.

Wataru Mori was a scholar of philosophy and other fields who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1951). He held posts at Tokyo Medical and Dental University (~1968–1973) and the University of Tokyo (~1973–1989).
Wataru Ryose is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under the doctoral supervision of Minoru Kiyota.

Wayne Chandira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, attested in 2026 as a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of Mark Rowe.

Wayne Proudfoot is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a Master of Theology and a PhD from Harvard University. He taught at Fordham University (~1968–1972) and became Professor of Religion at Columbia University circa 1972.

Wei Lin is a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology who earned a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. Lin worked as an archaeologist at Nanjing Municipal Museum and as an assistant professor at Transylvania University.
Wei Wu is a Buddhist studies scholar who founded the International Buddhist College. As of 2026, Wu serves as an associate professor and Director of Undergraduate Studies at Emory University.

Wei-Cheng Lin works in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Lin was a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill until 2015, before joining the faculty at the University of Chicago that same year.

Wei-jen Teng is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies who earned a PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil. Teng has held posts at DILA and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
